questions.stem: A planet has the same average density as the Earth but twice its radius. If the escape velocity from the Earth is $11.2\ \text{km s}^{-1}$, find the escape velocity from the planet in $\text{km s}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
**Key idea:** $v_e = \sqrt{2GM/R}$ and $M = \tfrac43\pi R^3 \rho$, so $v_e = R\sqrt{\tfrac83 \pi G\rho} \propto R$ at fixed density.

1. Radius doubles → $v_e$ doubles.
2. **$v_e = 22.4\ \text{km s}^{-1}$**
hints: Write the mass in terms of density and radius.
